questions.question: Identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes on shipping papers:

options.text: Can be shortened if you are using a small piece of paper.
Can be shortened to make them easier to read.
Can be shortened if the shortened versions are easy to understand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be shortened.
questions.explanation: Never shorten identification numbers, shipping names, or hazard classes on shipping papers. The only exception is if the hazardous materials regulations specifically allow that abbreviation.

questions.question: Using a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts you when you are speaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can distract you.
questions.explanation: Even with a hands-free phone, you can become mentally distracted. Talking takes your mind away from driving, which is just as dangerous as holding a phone.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, stopping distance:

options.text: Is longer than on a normal road.
Is shorter than on a normal road.
Is about the same as on a normal road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is longer than on a normal road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop on slippery surfaces because your tires have less grip on the road.

questions.question: Multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions are used to:

options.text: Make a vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra gears.
questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide additional gears.

questions.question: When braking a tractor-trailer with ABS, you should:

options.text: Use extra brake force to activate the ABS.
Use less brake pressure than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake a tractor-trailer with ABS the same way you would brake any other vehicle. Do not change your braking technique.

questions.question: To control liquid surge in a tank, a driver should:

options.text: Start braking well before you need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start braking well before you need to stop.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly and carefully with liquid tanks. Brake early and gradually before stops. Keep a safe distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle turns a corner:

options.text: The turn should be as tight as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should go over the curb.
It is okay to knock over street signs if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning. This is called off-tracking. It is especially noticeable with trailers.

questions.question: A truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer, you should:

options.text: Turn on air to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Follow the correct steps to couple and uncouple trailers safely. After connecting the air lines, turn on air to the trailer.

questions.question: When checking your tires, avoid finding:

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.
Valve stems that are not damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Different tire sizes.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two years.
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the carrier accepts the materials. For hazardous waste, the time is three years.

questions.question: Joggers wearing headsets may:

options.text: Usually be aware of what is happening around them.
Not be aware of what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Watch out for pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic sounds and may not know you are there.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts could be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check if the nuts are tight when you see rust in that area.

questions.question: To know which placards to use, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.
The types of containers holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: To choose the right hazardous materials placards, you must know the hazard class of the materials, how much is being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in the vehicle.

questions.question: A vehicle smaller than yours will usually:

options.text: Take longer to stop than your vehicle.
Take about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can usually stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far back to stay from other vehicles.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in wet weather when it is below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze, and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze, and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Using the parking brake in very wet, freezing weather can cause the brakes to freeze. This prevents the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: If Class 3 flammable liquids must be moved to another tank, they:

options.text: May be transferred on the roadway if no one else is nearby.
Should not be transferred on a public road unless there is an emergency.
Should be kept secret when moved to another tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be transferred on a public road unless there is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Do not transfer flammable liquids from one vehicle to another on a public road unless it is an emergency. Always warn others about the hazards of these materials.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Help a driver avoid wheel lockup.
Prevent a vehicle from accelerating uphill.
Prevent a vehicle from accelerating downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help a driver avoid wheel lockup.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: If you turn quickly to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Not brake because it may cause the wheels to lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not brake because it may cause the wheels to lock.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking can cause your wheels to lock and your vehicle to skid out of control.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials containers, you should not use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hooks.
questions.explanation: Protect containers of hazardous materials. Never use hooks or other equipment that could damage the containers or packaging.
